Why did @HyperliquidPC rate global stablecoins 5/5 for crypto trading, liquidity and DeFi access, but only 3/5 for everyday payments?

That surprised me.
Stables move 24/7, weekends included, no waiting for banking hours.

Personally, a card linked to your stablecoin balance makes daily spending easy. It works anywhere that takes @Visa or @Mastercard, even the small shops selling vegetables.

The payment still runs on traditional card rails, but spending straight from a stablecoin balance is useful to me.

Banks took some learning too. Using an exchange or neobank that supports stables can become just as familiar.

I get that 3/5 means neutral, but my own experience makes me curious about the reasoning behind that score.

That's my take. What about you?

The Everything Code comes out on November 3rd and I've got a favour to ask.

Ive spent 35 years trying to figure out how the world works... why the rules your parents lived by stopped working and why no matter how hard you work the gap keeps widening. Its not bad luck. It's debt, demographics and the debasement of money.

The book is everything I've learned about those forces. Why the system broke, what the central banks did about it, and what comes next... which is the Exponential Age, and its going to be the most disruptive and the most exciting thing any of us live through.

Most of you know this stuff already. But the people who really need it have never heard of me. The ones lying awake wondering why they can't get ahead. That's who I wrote this for.

The only way a book reaches those people is if it gets noticed in the first week. Pre-orders all land on day one. Thats what pushes it up the lists, gets it in front of people who dont follow me, and gets it into the hands of someone who has no idea why the world feels so rigged.

So if youre already planning to read it... please dont wait until November. Pre-order it now. It genuinely matters more than you'd think.

I've spent years on this and I think a lot of people need to understand it.

Help me get it out there. Thank you.

tweets.text:
This is my thesis: no one uses AI. I repeat, absolutely no one. We live in a bubble.

Even among my friends who pay for it, when I ask them to open ChatGPT and show me their queries, it’s the same handful of basic things.

Most don’t even know they can upload a photo and ask questions about it. Connecting Gmail so an agent can read and send emails blows their minds. An agent opening a browser and checking them into a flight? They’ve never even heard of it.

The massive challenge right now is adoption, and then getting people who already signed up to actually use what they’re paying for. Most have absolutely zero clue what’s possible.

Imagine the compute shortage when everyone starts using AI like the top 1% of users do today.

tweets.text:
I’m torn on this. I keep my agent memories in Google Drive and switch between Muse, ChatGPT and Grok Bots pretty easily. For me it mostly comes down to who gives me the most tokens and the best model in terms of speed and quality. Hard to see a moat there.

But I’m pretty sure the average consumer will never bother doing this. Then again, if you can just tell your new agent “log into Grok Bot and move my memories to Muse,” maybe they won’t have to.

My thesis is that software is becoming a commodity, so the model is the key. And the model increasingly comes down to who has more compute, which comes down to who has more money to spend on capex. The moat moves down the stack ladies and gentlemen
